Checked 2026-09-20. Heights are facts; the polygons are not redistributed here
city.height: ELEVATION - BASE_ELEVATION, feet converted to metres

ground.basis: footprints that passed the foot_ratio cross-check

fields.ground_z: median class-2 ground elevation, metres above the lidar datum
fields.gnd_in_dz: median class-2 height INSIDE the footprint relative to ground_z; a few metres negative is an excavated basement
fields.area_m2: area of OUR footprint polygon, EPSG:3857 corrected by cos(lat)
fields.match: how this building's footprint was found: snapshot_id (the inventory names the snapshot feature - identity, not proximity) or centroid (nearest polygon within 40 m). It decides what foot_ratio is worth, so read it first
fields.inv_area_m2: the inventory's own footprint area for the same building
fields.foot_ratio: area_m2 / inv_area_m2. 0.5-2.0 is fine; outside that our polygon is a fragment or the wrong building, and outside 0.25-3.5 no height is published at all. AN INDEPENDENT COMPARISON ONLY WHERE match=centroid: on a snapshot_id row the inventory measured the polygon we measure, so the ratio is the two formulas' constant 1.007 and says nothing. There it is city_cover and city_ratio - an outline drawn by somebody else - that test the footprint
fields.h_max: tallest class-6 point above ground_z, metres
fields.h_p99: 99th percentile of the same - the robust roof height
fields.h_med: median class-6 height - the bulk roof surface
fields.levels: [height_m, % of roof cells] roof steps, 0.5 m raster
fields.slope_med: median cell-to-cell slope of that raster, degrees
fields.fill: % of the raster's bounding box that carries any return
fields.roof: flat / pitched / mixed from the slope histogram
fields.roof_no: which guard declined a roof call: roof_too_small, too_sparse, raster_patchy, facade_not_roof, no_slope
fields.roof_conf: 0..1 confidence in that verdict. Capped at 0.45 when split_agree is false, at 0.6 on a partial footprint and at 0.45 on a late_build row (where the roof is the 2017 SITE's, not this building's), so the number can be read on its own
fields.split_agree: both random halves of the points gave the same verdict. This is REPEATABILITY, not correctness - a biased estimator agrees with itself - so it only lowers roof_conf
fields.noise_n: ASPRS class 7/18 returns dropped before measuring
fields.city_h: City of Austin 2017 footprint height, metres
fields.city_cover: fraction of OUR footprint that city polygon covers
fields.city_ratio: that city polygon's area divided by our footprint's. Above ~2 the city polygon is a whole block and its height is somebody else's building
fields.h_nv: 99th percentile of every non-vegetation, non-noise return inside the footprint. A QUESTION, never a height: well above h_max it is sometimes an unclassified roof and sometimes a crane, a neighbour's wall or a stray class-1 return. Nothing is derived from it
fields.snap_h: the snapshot's own final_height, for comparison only
fields.late_build: the snapshot height is >8 m above anything the 2017 lidar found here: this building was built after the flight and the heights above describe the SITE, not the building

caveats: lidar is nadir: this says nothing about walls and nothing about night
2017 flight: anything finished after 2017 is missing or half-built
